unsupported_claims: Graph factorization directly factorizes a graph proximity matrix.
This lets graph factorization preserve the global weighted structure of the Wikipedia link graph more faithfully than DeepWalk’s random-walk-based, local co-occurrence objective.
The graph is relatively sparse and the classification signal is strongly tied to explicit link structure, which favors matrix factorization over sampled walks.

Compared with LINE-based methods, graph factorization tends to capture higher-order proximity more effectively while still using the full graph information, whereas LINE mainly preserves first- or second-order local neighborhood relations.
Graph factorization produces embeddings that are more aligned with the class structure in Wikipedia pages, leading to better classification performance.
rationale: The source explicitly supports only the key point that graph factorization outperforms DeepWalk because DeepWalk ignores edge weights, and that LINE(2nd) is slightly better than graph factorization while LINE(1st+2nd) is best. The answer adds several extra mechanistic explanations and comparative claims about graph factorization and LINE that are not stated or directly entailed by the papers.
